# Final adjudication: position 28

Disposition: escalated-to-owner; source status verified. The item is untouched and retains its final rejected bytes. Inspected the complete statement/proof, Alpha response, both Terra rejections, owning batch-15 manifest, proof contract and risk record, current sweetness definition, sigma-directed lemma, the repaired density-transfer interface, published forcing-preorder and two-step-iteration definitions, and page context.

Terra's localization objection is valid: the second application of the density-transfer Statement needs a globally dense union, whereas only density below p_0 has been obtained. This alone is repairable, for example by adjoining a dummy family of conditions incompatible with p_0; their union with the locally dense family is globally dense, and the dummy family cannot supply a witness below p_0. This observation does not complete the item.

A separate claim is false for the raw admitted-pair carrier defined in Given. Take Q_1 to be a one-element forcing, Q_2={a,b} an antichain with equality order, and P_0 the one-element forcing embedded as Boolean top in each completion. Both forcings are sweet: D=Q and E_n=equality at every level satisfy directedness, sequential bounds and transfer directly. P_0 is a complete suborder of each nonzero completion: its singleton maximal antichain maps to Boolean top. Every pair is admitted, so O=Q_1 times Q_2 is a two-element antichain. No map from the one-element Q_1 into O preserves maximal antichains: its singleton image is not maximal in O. Thus O does not contain a complete canonical copy of Q_1. Step 7.1's 1_(Q_2) does not exist under the published def-forcing-preorder-compatibility-and-filter, which explicitly says a weakest condition need not exist.

This is a defect of the queued draft's presentation, not of that published definition. One could normalize the factors by adjoining weakest conditions, or formulate the embeddings at the Boolean-completion level, but the full extension-of-sweetness-model assertion must then be proved for the resulting presentation. I have not settled that full repair under the current five extension clauses. In particular step 8.1 merely refers to a source construction; it does not prove existence of a dense-open part disjoint from the fixed copy, nor the mixed transfer and extension clauses. The proposed deletion is not automatically dense (already a singleton factor can leave no outside part). Step 1.1 also applies the density-transfer lemma before its q-in-D hypothesis has been met. These cannot be certified by fixing the repeated-index or localization issue alone.

Authorities consulted: https://shelah.logic.at/files/95333/176.pdf — read Definition 7.2 and Claim 7.3 p.34, complete Lemma 7.5 pp.35–36, Claim 7.11 and Claim 7.12 pp.41–42, alongside the current library definitions. The source explicitly uses trivial/weakest coordinates for canonical copies and gives the extension argument by reference to the composition construction. It supports the intended theorem in its presentation but does not, as read, establish the raw-preorder assertion contradicted above. An additional web search for the exact extension claim returned the same primary paper; no aggregator or search snippet is used as proof.

Decision owed: specify the correct normalized amalgam/embedding interface compatible with arbitrary library forcing preorders, and supply or authorize a complete proof of the fixed-model extension clause (including degenerate factors and mixed transfer) for that interface.
